title: Energy-Drinks - Unexplored Long-Term Cardiovascular Alterations in TEens and TwEens-Study (EDUCATE-II)
summary:
Two-thirds of all children and adolescents consume energy drinks (ED). Approximately 12% of these minors show high chronic consumption patterns, corresponding to an average monthly consumption of about 7 liters of ED. 
Recent publications by our research group suggest unfavourable cardiovascular effects following acute ED-consumption. Data on the effects of high chronic ED-consumption on the pediatric cardiovascular system are not yet sufficient. 
The aim of the EDUCATE-II study is to systematically investigate this issue.

interventions.name:
"High chronic" ED consumers (≥4 ED-days/week since ≥12 months, caffeine intake from EDs of ≥3 mg/kg on the day of consumption), 
aged ≥14 and ≤21 years

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion in the case group (≥4 ED-days/week for ≥12 months, caffeine intake from EDs of ≥3 mg/kg on the day of consumption) 
or in the control group (no ED consumption)
Exclusion criteria:
Age <14 or >21 years
Known pre-existing health conditions that may affect cardiovascular function, regular intake of medications and/or drugs that may affect cardiovascular function, current pregnancy, acute infection
